1. The current $I$ through a resistor is measured with a digital ammeter to be 0.10 A. The uncertainty in the calculated value of $I^2$ will be
A. 1 %.
B. 2 %.
C. 5 %.
D. 20 %.

2.text_clean:
2. Joseph runs along a long straight track. The variation of his speed $v$ with time $t$ is shown below.
[Graph: v / m s$^{-1}$ (0 to 12) against t / s (0 to 30); speed rises linearly from 0 at t = 0 to 10 m s$^{-1}$ at t = 10 s, then constant at 10 m s$^{-1}$ to t = 30 s]
After 25 seconds Joseph has run 200 m. Which of the following is correct at 25 seconds?
Instantaneous speed / m s$^{-1}$ | Average speed / m s$^{-1}$
A. 8 m s$^{-1}$ | 8 m s$^{-1}$
B. 8 m s$^{-1}$ | 10 m s$^{-1}$
C. 10 m s$^{-1}$ | 8 m s$^{-1}$
D. 10 m s$^{-1}$ | 10 m s$^{-1}$

3.text_clean:
3. A skydiver of mass 80 kg falls vertically with a constant speed of 50 m s$^{-1}$. The upward force acting on the skydiver is approximately
A. 0 N.
B. 80 N.
C. 800 N.
D. 4000 N.

4.text_clean:
4. A particle of mass $m$ is moving with constant speed $v$ in uniform circular motion. What is the total work done by the centripetal force during one revolution?
A. Zero
B. $\frac{mv^2}{2}$
C. $mv^2$
D. $2\pi mv^2$

5.text_clean:
5. A cyclist rides around a circular track at a uniform speed. Which of the following correctly gives the net horizontal force on the cyclist at any given instant of time?
Net horizontal force along direction of motion | Net horizontal force normal to direction of motion
A. zero | zero
B. zero | non zero
C. non zero | zero
D. non zero | non zero

6.text_clean:
6. A solid piece of tungsten melts into liquid without a change in temperature. Which of the following is correct for the molecules in the liquid phase compared with the molecules in the solid phase?
Kinetic energy | Potential energy
A. same | greater
B. same | same
C. greater | greater
D. greater | same

7.text_clean:
7. A heater of constant power heats a liquid of mass $m$ and specific heat capacity $c$. The graph below shows how the temperature of the liquid varies with time.
[Graph: temperature against time; straight line with positive gradient starting from a non-zero temperature at time 0]
The gradient of the graph is $k$ and no energy is lost to the surroundings. What is the power of the heater?
A. $kmc$
B. $\frac{k}{mc}$
C. $\frac{mc}{k}$
D. $\frac{1}{kmc}$

8.text_clean:
8. Which of the following is equivalent to the principle of energy conservation?
A. Newton's first law
B. The first law of thermodynamics
C. Newton's second law
D. The second law of thermodynamics

[Graph: Pressure / $\times 10^5$ Pa (0 to 3) against Volume / $\times$ m$^3$ (0 to 1.5); P at (0.5, 3), Q at (1.5, 3), R at (1.5, 1); P→Q horizontal, Q→R vertical down, R→P straight line back to P]
Which of the following is the net work done by the gas in a cycle?
A. $4.5\times10^5$ J
B. $3.0\times10^5$ J
C. $1.0\times10^5$ J
D. Zero

[Graph: displacement against time; sinusoid starting at zero and first going negative (−sin shape), two cycles]
Which graph shows how the object's acceleration $a$ varies with time $t$?
[Four graphs of a against t: A. starts at positive maximum (cosine); B. starts at negative maximum (−cosine); C. starts at zero going negative (−sine); D. starts at zero going positive (sine)]

11. A transverse wave travels from left to right. The graph below shows how, at a particular instant of time, the displacement of particles in the medium varies with position. Which arrow represents the direction of the velocity of the particle marked P?
[Graph: displacement against position; sinusoidal wave; P lies just above the axis on a rising (positive-slope) section of the wave; arrows from P: A up, B right, C down, D left]

12.text_clean:
12. Light travels from air into glass as shown below.
[Diagram: incident ray in air makes 30° with the air–glass boundary; refracted ray in glass makes 80° with the boundary; dashed normal shown]
The refractive index of the glass is
A. $\frac{\sin 30^\circ}{\sin 80^\circ}$
B. $\frac{\sin 80^\circ}{\sin 30^\circ}$
C. $\frac{\sin 60^\circ}{\sin 10^\circ}$
D. $\frac{\sin 10^\circ}{\sin 60^\circ}$

13. The fundamental (first harmonic) frequency for a particular organ pipe is 330 Hz. The pipe is closed at one end but open at the other. What is the frequency of its next highest harmonic?
A. 110 Hz
B. 165 Hz
C. 660 Hz
D. 990 Hz

14.text_clean:
14. Light is diffracted at a single slit. Which of the following graphs best represents how the intensity $I$ of the diffracted light varies with the diffraction angle $\theta$?
[Four graphs of I against θ: A. equal-height broad sinusoidal maxima; B. equal-height narrow sharp peaks; C. tall central maximum with much smaller secondary maxima decreasing outwards; D. triangular peak at θ = 0]

15.text_clean:
15. Light of wavelength $\lambda$ is emitted by two point sources. The light passes through a circular aperture of diameter $b$ and is received by an observer. The angular separation of the sources from the observer's position is $\theta$. The sources are **not** resolved by the observer. Which of the following mathematical relationships applies?
[Diagram: sources S$_1$ and S$_2$ subtending angle θ at an aperture of diameter b, observer just behind the aperture]
A. $\theta < 1.22\frac{\lambda}{b}$
B. $\theta > 1.22\frac{\lambda}{b}$
C. $\theta = 1.22\frac{\lambda}{b}$
D. $\theta = \frac{\lambda}{b}$

16.text_clean:
16. Plane-polarized light is incident normally on a polarizer which is able to rotate in the plane perpendicular to the light as shown below.
[Diagram 1: incident light (intensity = 8 W m$^{-2}$) passes through a polarizer; transmitted light (intensity = 2 W m$^{-2}$). Diagram 2: same incident light (intensity = 8 W m$^{-2}$), polarizer rotated; transmitted light intensity not given]
In diagram 1, the intensity of the incident light is 8 W m$^{-2}$ and the transmitted intensity of light is 2 W m$^{-2}$. Diagram 2 shows the polarizer rotated 90° from the orientation in diagram 1. What is the new transmitted intensity?
A. 0 W m$^{-2}$
B. 2 W m$^{-2}$
C. 6 W m$^{-2}$
D. 8 W m$^{-2}$

17.text_clean:
17. One electronvolt is equal to
A. $1.6\times10^{-19}$ C.
B. $1.6\times10^{-19}$ J.
C. $1.6\times10^{-19}$ V.
D. $1.6\times10^{-19}$ W.
17.note: eV definition; 2009 syllabus places it under electric potential difference (T5) -> B.5 (could also be D.2).

[Circuit: 5.0 V cell in series with a 10 kΩ fixed resistor (top) and an LDR (bottom); voltmeter V connected across the LDR]
The voltmeter reads 3.0 V. Which of the following changes would cause the reading on the voltmeter to increase?
A. Swapping the positions of the LDR and the fixed resistor
B. Increasing the resistance of the fixed resistor
C. Increasing the amount of light shining on the LDR
D. Decreasing the amount of light shining on the LDR

19.text_clean:

A. rate of change of magnetic flux linkage.
B. rate of change of the magnetic flux through the coil.
C. change of magnetic flux linkage.
D. change of the magnetic flux through the coil.

A. $2VI$
B. $\sqrt{2}VI$
C. $VI$
D. $\frac{VI}{2}$

A. Into the page
B. Out of the page
C. To the left
D. To the right
